turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good morning, Miss Tan. I'm Dr. Liew, the anesthesiologist who'll be taking care of you during your surgery today. I just need to go through a few questions to make sure everything goes smoothly for your laparoscopic ovarian cystectomy. Is that okay with you?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Yes, doctor. I'm ready. Been waiting for this for weeks already lah.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Great. Let's start with your medical history. Can you tell me a bit about the ovarian cyst? When did you first notice symptoms?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: About three months ago, I had really bad lower tummy pain, like cramps but worse. My gynae did an ultrasound and found the cyst. They said it's about 6cm, so they want to remove it before it gets bigger or causes more trouble.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Understood. Now, let's go through your medications. You're on amlodipine for your blood pressure, right? What dose are you taking?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Yes, amlodipine 5mg once daily in the morning. And my birth control pills, levonorgestrel and ethinyl estradiol, same time every day. Oh, and I stopped doxycycline two weeks ago because of the surgery.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thank you. Now, about allergies – your records say 'no known allergies,' but I always like to double-check. Have you ever had a reaction to any antibiotics, particularly sulfa-based medications like co-trimoxazole or sulfadiazine?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Oh! Actually, yes. When I was a teenager, I took some sulfa pills for a skin infection and broke out in a terrible rash all over my body. It was really scary. I've avoided all sulfa drugs since then.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thank you for sharing that. I'll make sure to note your sulfa allergy clearly in your chart. Now, have you eaten or drunk anything since midnight? We need to confirm your NPO status for general anesthesia.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, doctor. I had my last sip of water at 7am. Just like the instructions said.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Excellent. Any previous surgeries or anesthesia? Even minor procedures like stitching or dental work?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, this is my first time. I'm a bit nervous about the general anesthesia, to be honest.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: It's normal to feel that way. Finally, can you tell me about your daily activities? For example, can you walk up stairs or carry groceries without getting short of breath?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Yes, I walk to work every day and climb five flights of stairs. No problems at all. I'm quite active, lah.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: That's reassuring. We'll make sure your blood pressure is well-controlled during surgery since you're on amlodipine. Any other concerns before we proceed?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, I think that's all. Thank you for explaining everything so clearly, doctor.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: My pleasure, Miss Tan. We'll take good care of you. The nursing team will come for you shortly. See you in the operating theater.
